M/S Iffcotokio General Insurance ... vs Kandala Ilaiah on 19
June, 2023
Author: Lalitha Kanneganti

Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1865 of 2009
Judgment:

The appellant insurance company - respondent no.2 has filed the present appeal aggrieved by the order and decree dated 24.11.2008 passed in O.P.No.452 of 2006 by the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District, N.T.R.Nagar.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District, N.T.R.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Having heard Mr. K.S.N.Murthy, learned counsel for the appellant insurance company and Mr.
V.Atchuta Ram, perused the entire material on record.

3. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident that occurred on 09.04.2006 and the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.3,83,926/-.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that on 09.04.2006 when the petitioner has boarded in an auto, the driver drove the auto at high speed in rash and negligent LK, J MACMA_1865_2009 manner, lost control over the vehicle and as a result, the auto turned turtle due to which the petitioner and other inmates of the auto received injuries.
The Tribunal having considered Ex.A5 i.e., disability certificate, the petitioner has sustained 80% disability.

He was working as Hamali, due to accident,
he sustained multiple fractures i)D-12 wedge compensation fracture ii) fracture of paraplegia and bladder and bower involvement iii) fracture inferior dislocation left shoulder iv) fracture of superior and inferior public ramie right side v) multiple bleeding injuries all over the body.
Because of the said injuries he is not able to do his daily work and he also lost his daily earnings.
The doctor deposed that all the injuries are grave in nature and as the petitioner suffers spinal chord injury, he was suffering 80% permanent partial disability and marked Ex.A5.
As per Ex.A5 medical board has certified that the claimant is suffering from 80% disability due to Post Traumatic Paraplegia.

Further the claim of the petitioner was that he was earning an amount of Rs.6,000/- per month, but the LK, J MACMA_1865_2009 Court has taken his income as Rs.66/- per day and applying multiplier 17 has granted compensation of Rs.3,23,136/- towards loss of income due to 80%
permanent disability, Rs.5,000/- granted for each grievous injury and an amount of Rs.20,000/-
under the head of pain and suffering and for medical expenditure granted an amount of Rs.28,790/-
basing on Ex.A5 to Ex.A10.

For extra nourishment Rs.5,000/- and Rs.2,000/- towards transport,
loss of amenities Rs.5,000/- and granted a claim of Rs.3,83,926/-.

sentences.text: The case of the claimant is that he was working as Hamali, because of the injuries sustained by him now he is not in a position to work.

The disability certificate shows that he has suffered 80%
disability because of the injuries sustained by him and because of spinal chord injury he is not in a position to discharge his duties as Hamali.

In that case though it is stated by the doctor as 80%,
taking into consideration the occupation of the claimant the Court can straightly conclude that the disability can be taken as 100%.

Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation for the following reasons (i) as the driver of the vehicle is having LMV license, he is driving Heavy Motor Vehicle ii) as he is covered by the employees trade insurance and as per the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act') there is bar under Section 53 of Employees' State Insurance Act to file application under any other acts.
iii) the age of the claimant was 33 years and multiplier that applies is 16, but the Court below has applied 17.
He also submits that the Court having applied multiplier ought not to have granted any compensation for the injuries.
He also submits that the application under the Act itself is not maintainable and compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is excessive.

7. Coming to the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that without there being any cross appeal, the respondents cannot seek any enhancement or LK, J MACMA_1865_2009 they can urge anything on the aspect of enhancement, this Court is of the view that this act being beneficial legislation when Insurance Company is questioning the quantum along with liability and while addressing the same if it comes to the notice of this Court that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not reasonable, this Court can as well consider the same without there being any fault.
Hence, this Court is deposing to consider the said aspect whether the compensation was just and reasonable.
8. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that he has not filed any cross objections.

However, as the Insurance Company is questioning the quantum along with liability this Act being beneficial legislation, the Court without there being any cross appeal while appreciating the said aspect of compensation looked into aspect of compensation.
He also submits that the accident has happened in the year 2006 and he was earning an amount of Rs.6,000/-.
The Court has only considered Rs.66/- per day.

He submitted that in the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of LK, J MACMA_1865_2009 Ramachandrappa Vs. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance1, as the petitioner was working as Hamali, the Court below ought to have considered Rs.4,500/- as income and granted compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Even under the heads of pain and suffering, extra nourishment,
attendent charges and amounts that were granted by the Tribunal were not just and reasonable.

9. The contention of the Insurance Company is that there is bar under Section 53 of the Employees'
State Insurance Act and he also relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Western India Plywood Ltd vs. Shri. P. Ashokan and submits that when once he is covered under Insurance Act,
they cannot maintain application under Section 53 of the Employees' State Insurance Act.

2 appropriate to look at 53 which reads as follows:
"Section 53: Bar against receiving or recovery of compensation or damages under any other law:
An insured person or his dependants shall not be entitled to receive or recover,
whether from the employer of the insured person or from any other person, any compensation or damages under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 or any other law for the time (2011) 13 SCC 236 LK, J MACMA_1865_2009 being in force or otherwise, in respect of an employment injury sustained by the insured person as an employee under this Act".
10.

entities.text: M/S Iffcotokio General Insurance ... vs Kandala Ilaiah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is very clear from the said provision that this is applicable to the injuries sustained by the employee in the course of employment but not in the motor vehicle accident.
Hence, this Court is of the view that Section 53 of Employees' State Insurance Act will not come to the rescue of the Insurance Company.

11. In the light of the Mukund Dewangan vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited2, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation though the driver was driving the Heavy Motor Vehicle having license of Light Motor Vehicle.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. The Tribunal has taken into consideration the income of claimant as Rs.66 /- per day.

As the petitioner was working as Hamali he was earning Rs.6,000/- per month, the monthly income of the petitioner can be taken as Rs.4,500/- in the light of the law laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ramachandrappa's Case.

When the aspect of disability comes, a certificate has been issued by the Medical board assessing the 2017 14 SCC 663 LK, J MACMA_1865_2009 disability of the petitioner @ 80%, but the Tribunal without any discussion has considered it as 80%.
On the face of it, it appears that the said conclusion of the Tribunal is without any application of mind.
Further, if the age of the petitioner is 33, the correct multiplier to be adopted is 16, whereas the Tribunal has applied the multiplier 17.

Hence, this Court is of the view that the disability has to be taken @ 100%
and as far as the multiplier is concerned, appropriate multiplier for the age of 33 is '16'.
If the income is taken as Rs.4,500/- and future prospects at 40%, the monthly income of the petitioner comes to Rs.6,300/-(4,500+1,800).
Hence, under the head of loss of income due to permanent disability, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.12,09,600/- (6300x12x16).
13. Further, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.10,000/- for extra nourishment and the petitioner is also entitled for medical bills @ Rs.28,790/-.
14. Under the head of pain and suffering, the Tribunal has not granted any amount.
Hence, under the head of pain and suffering that was undergone by the petitioner, Rs.50,000/- would be an appropriate amount.
LK, J MACMA_1865_2009

sentences.text: 3 15. In addition, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/- each towards attendant charges and transport charges.
Further, under legal expenses, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.10,000/-.
16. In the light of the above mentioned discussion, the appellant is entitled for compensation on the following amounts:

Head Compensation awarded (1) Loss of Income due to  permanent disability Rs.12,09,600 (2) Medical bills and future surgery Rs.28,790 (3) Pain and suffering Rs.50,000 (4) Extra nourishment Rs.10,000 (5) Attendant benefits Rs.10,000 (6) Transport charges Rs.10,000 (7) Legal expenses Rs.10,000 (8) Total compensation awarded Rs.13,28,390/-
17.

In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.3,83,926/- to Rs.13,28,390 /-.
LK, J MACMA_1865_2009
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The claimants shall pay the court fee on the enhanced amount of compensation.
(c) The Insurance company/Corporation shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
___________________________ LALITHA KANNEGANTI, J Date: 19.06.2023 vsl/sa LK, J MACMA_1865_2009 THE HON'BLE SMT.
